comparison: Strong agreement on independent function of βH-Spec and α-Spec (C3, C53-C55, C58-C64, C98-C100). Both evaluations treat the localization data, RNAi experiments, and PLA results as compelling evidence for this major finding that challenges classical views. Jaccard index: 0.923.

Strong agreement on reciprocal antagonism between βH-Spec and myosin (C5, C72-C76, C112-C113). Both evaluations affirm the mutual exclusivity and reciprocal regulation as well-supported by the data. Peer reviewers describe the experimental flow as 'logical.' Jaccard index: 0.875.

Strong agreement on co-localization of βH-Spec with myosin and F-actin (C4, C66-C69). Both evaluations accept the quantitative Pearson correlation data. Peer reviewers implicitly endorse the measurements by praising the quantification methods. Jaccard index: 0.833.

Strong agreement on distinct mechanisms for α-Spec and βH-Spec (C107-C111). Both evaluations accept the differential effects on epithelial thickness and the proposed mechanistic explanations, though OpenEval notes the α-Spec mechanism is more speculative. Jaccard index: 0.833.

Strong agreement on βH-Spec overexpression effects (C78-C84). Both evaluations praise the CRISPR-based overexpression approach and accept the reciprocal effects on myosin, tension, Jub recruitment, and wing size as supporting the competition model. Jaccard index: 0.75.

Strong agreement on genetic epistasis showing Jub-dependent mechanism (C41-C49, C96-C97). Both evaluations affirm that jub knockdown suppresses spectrin knockdown effects on wing size and Hippo signaling. Peer reviewers specifically praise the epistasis analysis. Jaccard index: 0.667.

Strong agreement on competition mechanism from in vitro and modeling data (C6, C87-C89, C114-C117). Both evaluations accept the co-sedimentation assays and structural modeling as supporting F-actin competition. OpenEval notes experimental limitations while peer reviewers highlight novelty of the mechanism. Jaccard index: 0.667.

Strong agreement on structural modeling showing overlapping binding sites (C91-C93). Both evaluations accept the modeling approach and conclusions about steric interference. No concerns raised by either evaluation. Jaccard index: 0.6.

Strong agreement on increased myosin and tension upon spectrin knockdown (C34-C37). Both evaluations explicitly note this contradicts previous reports and treat the data as 'compelling.' Peer reviewers praise tissue specificity and quantitative methods. OpenEval also addresses C40, C94-C95 not covered in this peer result. Jaccard index: 0.444.

Strong agreement on mechanistic model for coordination of contraction and stabilization (C8, C122, C130-C131). Both evaluations support the proposed mechanism linking competition to ratcheting phenomena. Peer reviewers note relevance to other systems. OpenEval also addresses C126-C129. Jaccard index: 0.364.

Strong agreement on β-Spec dependence for α-Spec localization (C56-C57, C101). Both evaluations accept the RNAi data showing asymmetric dependence. OpenEval additionally addresses mechanistic explanation (C102-C103) not explicitly covered in peer result. Jaccard index: 0.333.

Both address increased Jub recruitment upon spectrin knockdown (C40, C95). OpenEval groups this with myosin/tension data (R1), while peer reviewers treat it as a separate key finding (R2) that reconciles conflicting literature. Both strongly support the finding. Jaccard index: 0.222.

Partial overlap on α-Spec effects (C50-C51). OpenEval addresses α-Spec increasing Jub recruitment and epistasis with jub knockdown. Peer R2 focuses on broader epistasis analysis including α-Spec. Both support the findings. Jaccard index: 0.2.

Minimal overlap (C51 only). OpenEval R3 addresses α-Spec effects on Jub and phenotypes. Peer R3 focuses on broader epistasis analysis. Both support Jub-dependent regulation but address different aspects. Jaccard index: 0.091.

Minimal overlap (C45 only). OpenEval R2 addresses broad epistasis analysis including tension manipulation. Peer R12 specifically addresses this tension manipulation experiment. Both support the findings. Jaccard index: 0.091.

Minimal overlap on PLA data (C63). OpenEval R15 specifically evaluates PLA experiments with methodological caveats. Peer R4 addresses broader independent function evidence including PLA. Both support the findings. Jaccard index: 0.077.

Minimal overlap (C7 only). OpenEval R11 addresses mechanistic interpretation of competition model. Peer R9 addresses broader mechanistic implications including ratcheting. Both strongly support the competition mechanism. Jaccard index: 0.125.

OpenEval R14 addresses prior literature claims (C31-C33) about previous reports and contradictions with established principles. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background/context claims.
OpenEval R16 addresses background literature on conformational regulation (C118-C121). These are context claims rather than new findings. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
